ICS: Resident asked if we could discuss smoking/referral to the Quitline.
Resident provided information about smoking and/or the Quitline.
Resident asked me about my smoking and what my triggers are. (If smoking habits are addressed but triggers are not, give credit and make a comment in the comment box**.)**
Resident encouraged me to talk about what would be the positive and negative aspects of quitting smoking (Your motivation or lack of motivation).
Resident asked me how I felt about accepting referral to the Quitline.
Resident was empathetic (they gave me reflective statements, for example, “you cut down while you were pregnant, that must have been hard?”).
Resident summarized at the end? (This should be specific to your motivation to quit.)
The examinee greeted me appropriately.   a. The examinee introduces him/her self  b. The examinee explained his/her role  c. The examinee addressed me by name
Expressed interest in me as a person.   a. Showed interest in me as a “person”, not just my issue/concern  b. Explored my reaction to the illness or problem/impact on my life

The examinee listened and paid attention to me.   a. Non-verbal expression of interest: (body language, nodding, eye contact)  b. Note-taking was balanced with conversation and eye contact  c. The examines did not talk down to me  d. The examinee summarized information and/or repeated information given  by me during the encounter

The examinee encouraged me to tell my story.   a. History was collected in an organized fashion  b. Used words I could understand and explained any technical terms in plain language  c. The examinee asked a combination of open-ended questions and focused questions  d. The examinee did not unnecessarily interrupt me

The examinee included me in the decision making.   a. Elicited my perspective on the issue at hand  b. Encouraged questions: asked if I had any questions or concerns  c. Explored my concerns about willingness/ability to accomplish the follow-up plan

The examinee was emotionally supportive.   a. Statements of empathy and/or support were expressed  b. The examinee validated my concerns/emotions  c. Non-verbal expression of concern/empathy (for example: nodding, facial expression, eye  contact)
I would return to the examinee for future care.
Supported you for cutting down (not been judgmental because you didn’t fully quit).
Assessed your readiness to quit (on a scale from 1 – 10).
Explain some of the impact of second hand and third hand smoke for children, including asthma, pneumonia, sudden infant death syndrome, ear infections, hospitalization, respiratory infections.
If you refuse referral, the trainee should leave the conversation open to restarting at a later time.
PBLI: What do you think went well during the patient interview?
What would you have done differently?
